<p></p>
<p dir="auto">Bad decision!<br>
Why?<br>
When this field is again required, European webshop owners get in troubles.<br>
Because a telephone number IS private and nothing just to "share" because this value is requried.<br>
The more, if a website intends to collect such data, it has to be very good argumented, e.g. required because of our delivery serice, or because my grandma may wants to call you once ..</p>
<p dir="auto">This behaviour violates the GDPR!</p>
<p dir="auto">Instead add a new setting to make it either required or optional.<br>

<p dir="auto">By doing that, it will affect all payment and shipping details where payment and service providers may either or not require this field since a single change from each stores could affect the entire telephone field.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">If (and only then IF) any payment or shipping extension will need the telephone number (and I do not know any), the telephone number can be "collected".<br>
But, this has to be stated public (e.g. in the "Privacy Statement") and clear why this private and personal data is required.</p>
<p dir="auto">I see no reason for any payment provider to become telephone numbers (and I don't know one).<br>
Shipping couriers may need them, but only "may".</p>
<p dir="auto">Adding such advices into the help field at this setting, will help store owners to find their right decision.</p>

<p dir="auto">You can enable phone number collection in Checkout if you need to collect a phone number for shipping or invoicing.</p>

<p dir="auto">Means, IF it is required, it can be collected (and this has to be stated clearly in the "Privacy Statement" > why and who is receiving it for which purpose).</p>
<p dir="auto">I have made several plugins for PayPal (and other payment providers).<br>

data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">You have hightlighted only Stripe - and they say, it's <strong>optional</strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">And I wrote (from my experience the last 12 years) that no payment provider really need it (as required).<br>
Possible that some shipping couriers want it, but this can be only an option - none of them ever had the need to call me (and to be true, they have not the time to make a call).</p>
<p dir="auto">Daniels commit has all options: enable/disable this field, make it required or not.</p>
<p dir="auto">But it's the same with the birthdate: this can be a field some payment providers really need to evaluate the creditability of the customer (in case for example when an option to pay per "Credit" is given and selected).</p>
<p dir="auto">Those extensions have to offer automatically that field - or they are not worth to use in a webstore!<br>
In such cases the store owners would have the need to create a ** Custom Field** which value has to be submitted with that request - but that requries some extra coding.</p>
<p dir="auto">So, I would say, whenever an payment or shipping extension may require the telephone field, the extension developer has to add it in his extension.<br>
Basically a simple task ..</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Beside this discussion, I have some clients they need the telephone number because their products have to be discussed by phone before sold (and they argument this in their privacy statement very well - why and what for).</p>
<p dir="auto">On the other side, in 99% of all my clients from the European Market (and here especially DE and AT), wether they need the telephone number - nor they want it.<br>
Had to create extra for that a 3-line-extension to disable and hide it.</p>
<p dir="auto">So, to have such (new) options is a benefit I think.<br>
OpenCart must increase the market share and should have unique settings other store software does not have.<br>
Using OC only in China, India, USA cannot be the target, the store owners which have money, are sitting in Europe.</p>
<p dir="auto">And - as you may know - the restrictions in Ecommerce are here given in many ways.<br>
While Europe has the GDPR - all 27 countries have differences in their laws, it's not only the GDPR which has to be carefully implemented, the stores must have also an eye on the national regulations they have!</p>
<p dir="auto">Because punishments could be per case up to 100.000,- Euro in some special cases (even for really small shops selling only in their own country).<br>
And who is willing - or able - to pay such fines .. ?!</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li
